title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Heading (pencil, partly legible): cohomology of simplicial sets and canonical simplicial resolutions.

Setup. Let k be a ring and M a k-module. Suppose we are given a functor C^* from simplicial sets to cochain complexes of k-modules such that:
(a) for every simplicial set X there is an isomorphism H^*(X,M) ≅ H^*(C^*(X)), natural in X (and apparently in M);
(b) for each n, the functor X ↦ C^n(X) turns colimits into limits.

Step 1: representability. Condition (b) means each C^n is representable: C^n(X) = Hom(X, C^n_*), where C^n_m := C^n(Δ_m). So C^*_* is a cochain complex of simplicial k-modules.

Step 2: the Poincaré lemma. Take X = Δ_m in (a). Since Δ_m is contractible, C^*_m is a resolution of M. Hence M_* → C^*_* is a resolution of the constant simplicial module M_*, functorial in M.

Step 3: what else is needed. Grothendieck asks what forces H^*(C^*(X)) → H^*(X,M) to be an isomorphism for every X. Write Z^1_* for the 1-cocycles, so there is an exact sequence 0 → M_* → C^0_* → Z^1_* → 0. Applying H^*(X,−) gives
H^0(X,C^0_*) → H^0(X,Z^1_*) → H^1(X,M) → H^1(X,C^0_*) → H^1(X,Z^1_*),
with the first map marked 'épi' and the last marked 'inj'.

In (a), H^1(C^*(X)) is computed by cocycles modulo coboundaries, i.e. coker(H^0(X,C^0_*) → H^0(X,Z^1_*)). So H^1(X,M) is computed correctly as soon as H^1(X,C^0_*) = 0. Iterating, one needs the C^n_* to be 'flasque', meaning H^{>0}(X,C^n_*) = 0 for all X. In modern terms this is the extendability condition: restriction from Δ_m to its boundary or horns is surjective. Thus (a) is roughly equivalent to: each C^n_* is acyclic/flasque, and C^*_* resolves M.

Step 4 (NB). If C^*_* is a flasque resolution of M_*, the cocycle objects Z^i(C^*_*) are Eilenberg–MacLane simplicial modules K(M,i). Indeed Z^i(X) = Hom(X, Z^i_*) represents the i-cocycles.

Purpose. This is an axiomatic characterization of 'cochain theories' of simplicial sets via simplicial cochain objects. It is preparatory to divided-power de Rham / polynomial-forms models (Sullivan's A_PL), as the next page on minimal models confirms.
errors: No genuine errors visible. One gap: (a) with X = Δ_m gives only acyclicity of C^*(Δ_m). The needed flasqueness (H^i(X,C^n_*) = 0, i.e. extendability) is a separate hypothesis. The page seems to recognise this ('a) ... flasques ... suffisant ...') rather than claiming it follows from (a) alone.
Exactness on the right of the displayed long exact sequence needs H^1(X,C^0_*) = 0; the 'inj' annotation implicitly presupposes this.

ideas.what: Functors from simplicial sets to cochain complexes sending colimits to limits are represented by a cochain complex of simplicial modules C^*_* (C^n(X) = Hom(X, C^n_*)).
ideas.modern_name: Representability of cochain functors by simplicial cochain algebras (Sullivan–de Rham / Thom–Whitney formalism)

ideas.what: A simplicial cochain complex computes cohomology iff it satisfies a Poincaré lemma (it resolves M) and each degree is flasque/extendable.
ideas.modern_name: Poincaré lemma + extendability criterion ('simplicial de Rham theorem')

ideas.what: The cocycle objects Z^i of a flasque resolution are Eilenberg–MacLane simplicial modules K(M,i).

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard axiomatic rederivation of the Poincaré-lemma-plus-extendability criterion for simplicial cochain algebras, already in Sullivan, Bousfield–Gugenheim and Cartan around the same date. It is a nice converse-flavoured framing (any colimit-to-limit cochain theory is of this form), but it is well known.
